"Replace string-formatted SQL with a parameterized query using the DB-API `execute(sql, params)` form. Do NOT use f-strings or % formatting in the SQL string. Keep the SQL text identical except for replacing interpolated values with placeholders.\n"
"Prefer the Django ORM (`.filter()`, `.get()`). If raw SQL is unavoidable, use `cursor.execute(sql, [params])` or `RawSQL(sql, params)`. Never interpolate into the SQL string.\n"
"Use `text()` with bound parameters (`:name`) and pass values via `.execute(stmt, {\"name\": value})`. Do not concatenate.\n"
"Replace `Statement` + string concat with `PreparedStatement` and positional `?` placeholders. Bind each user-controlled value with the typed setter (`setString`, `setInt`, ...).\n"
"Use `jdbcTemplate.query(sql, args, rowMapper)` or `NamedParameterJdbcTemplate`. Remove all `+` concat in SQL.\n"
"Use the driver's placeholder syntax (`?` for mysql2, `$1` for pg) and pass values as the second argument array. Remove all template-literal interpolation from the query string.\n"
"Use `SqlCommand` with `@param` placeholders and `cmd.Parameters.AddWithValue()`. Remove string concat.\n"

"If parameterization is impossible (e.g., dynamic table/column name), validate the value against a hardcoded allowlist of permitted identifiers BEFORE building the query. Reject anything not in the allowlist.\n"
"Improper Neutralization of Data within a Query (e.g. JQL)"

"Stop building the query with an f-string / % / + concatenation of user-controlled values. If the client library supports bound parameters or a structured query builder, use it. If the target query language (e.g. Atlassian JQL) has no parameter binding, escape every interpolated value for the query's string context (e.g. replace `\"` with `\\\\\"` and `\\\\` with `\\\\\\\\`) AND validate it against a strict allowlist of permitted characters/identifiers before interpolation. Keep the query text identical except for the now-escaped/validated value.\n"

"If neither parameter binding nor reliable escaping is available, validate every user-controlled value against a hardcoded allowlist of permitted identifiers/characters BEFORE building the query and reject anything that does not match. Do not attempt to sanitize by stripping characters.\n"

"JQL (and similar query languages) have no DB-API placeholder binding, so the safe fix is strict allowlist validation + context-correct escaping of the interpolated value, mirroring the CWE-89 approach.\n"

"Replace `os.system` / `subprocess.*` with `shell=True` by a `subprocess.run([...], shell=False)` call where the command and each argument are separate list elements. User input must be a single list element, never concatenated into a string.\n"
"Use `new ProcessBuilder(List<String>)` with each argument as a separate element. Never pass a single concatenated string to `Runtime.exec(String)`.\n"
"Replace `child_process.exec()` with `execFile(cmd, [args])` or `spawn(cmd, [args])`. User input goes into the args array only.\n"
"Validate user input against `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$` (or a tighter domain-specific allowlist) before it reaches the command. Reject on mismatch; do not sanitize.\n"
"Remove `|safe`, `mark_safe()`, or `autoescape off` around the tainted variable. If HTML is genuinely required, sanitize with `bleach.clean()` using an explicit tag/attr allowlist.\n"
"Ensure the template uses `{{ var }}` (auto-escaped), not `{{ var|safe }}` or `Markup()`. For JSON-in-script contexts use `tojson` filter.\n"
"Remove `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`. Render the value as a text child (`{value}`). If HTML is required, sanitize with DOMPurify before assignment.\n"
"Replace `.innerHTML = x` with `.textContent = x`. For attribute sinks use `setAttribute` with a validated value.\n"
"Wrap the tainted value with the OWASP Java Encoder appropriate to context: `Encode.forHtml()`, `Encode.forHtmlAttribute()`, `Encode.forJavaScript()`.\n"
"The fix MUST match the output context (HTML body vs attribute vs JS string vs URL). Include the detected context in the prompt.\n"
"Resolve the user path against a fixed base directory, then verify the resolved absolute path is still inside the base. Reject (raise) if not. Do not strip \"../\" — resolve instead.\n"

"base = pathlib.Path(BASE_DIR).resolve()
target = (base / user_path).resolve()
if base not in target.parents and target != base:
    raise PermissionError("path escapes base dir")

"`File f = new File(BASE, userPath).getCanonicalFile();` then check `f.getPath().startsWith(BASE.getCanonicalPath())`.\n"
"`const target = path.resolve(BASE, userPath);` then reject if `!target.startsWith(path.resolve(BASE) + path.sep)`.\n"

"Replace `pickle.loads` / `yaml.load` with a safe equivalent: `json.loads` for data, or `yaml.safe_load`. If pickle is unavoidable, restrict with a custom `Unpickler.find_class` allowlist of permitted types.\n"
"Use an `ObjectInputFilter` (JEP 290) with an explicit class allowlist. Reject all classes not on the list. Prefer replacing Java serialization with JSON (Jackson) entirely.\n"
"Replace `BinaryFormatter` / `LosFormatter` / `NetDataContractSerializer` with `System.Text.Json`. If polymorphism needed, use a type discriminator allowlist.\n"

"Parse the URL, then enforce: (1) scheme in {https, http}, (2) host in an explicit allowlist (exact match or suffix match on owned domains), (3) resolved IP is NOT private/loopback/ link-local/metadata (169.254.0.0/16). Reject before request.\n"
"Do NOT fix by string-matching \"localhost\"/\"127.0.0.1\" — DNS rebinding and decimal/octal IP encodings bypass it. Resolve and check the IP.\n"
"Replace `xml.etree` / `lxml.etree` parse calls with the `defusedxml` drop-in equivalent, OR set `parser.resolve_entities = False` and disable DTD loading.\n"

"On the factory, set FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING true and disallow-doctype-decl true; set external-general-entities and external-parameter-entities false; setXIncludeAware(false); setExpandEntityReferences(false).\n"

"Accept only same-origin relative paths (must start with \"/\" and NOT \"//\" or \"/\\\\\"), OR validate the host against an explicit allowlist after URL parsing. Reject everything else and redirect to a safe default.\n"

"Replace the literal with a read from environment variable or the project's existing secret manager. Add the env-var name to the patch description. Do NOT generate or guess a new secret value. Flag the old value for rotation in the finding notes.\n"
"Requires data migration (re-hash on next login). Emit guidance describing bcrypt/argon2id with work-factor and the lazy-upgrade pattern. Do not emit a code patch.\n"

"Authorization fixes require knowledge of the intended policy. Never auto-generate a patch. Emit guidance pointing to the resource, the missing check, and the project's existing authz helper (if detected).\n"
